tags: The live board is the first screen
features: The product is the first screen, so a buyer sees what it does before reading a word
At 07:40 a job slips and the board prices it, so the value shows up in pounds rather than adjectives
The visitor takes, keeps or undoes the crew swap, so they make the coordinator’s call themselves
Pricing laid out as a monthly statement that does the maths, and a walkthrough booking that remembers the slot
name: Cadence
short: Route and shift software that prices every late job and lets your coordinator make the call.
long: Cadence opens on its own live board. Scroll and the clock ticks to 07:40, a job slips behind a crash and the board proposes a crew swap you take or leave. Then three features cut from the real screens, a pricing statement that does the maths and a walkthrough booking.
proves: Software can be sold by letting people use it on the first screen.
story: Route and shift software for cold-chain field crews. The board is not a screenshot: scroll and a shift plays out, a job slips behind a crash on the A629, and you decide whether to move the crew.
